name: Large Canadian medical laboratory and health services company
modelled_on: A large Ontario community laboratory company owned by a US laboratory group (name withheld), from its public web pages and filings
sector: health care: medical laboratory testing and health services
summary: This file models a large Canadian medical laboratory and health services company, built from public information about the model laboratory, a Ontario-based subsidiary of a US laboratory group with about 3,300 employees in 2022. Its largest business is community laboratory testing: about 200 collection centres in Ontario, Quebec and Manitoba take specimens from patients sent by community clinicians, couriers carry them to regional laboratories, and results go back to clinicians' EMRs and to a patient portal. Ontario pays for insured tests per test up to a company cap, Manitoba pays for its residents, and patients pay for uninsured tests and most Quebec community testing. Around this core the company runs separate business lines: a courier network, mobile collection in long-term care and retirement homes, specialised reference testing for more than 500 hospitals, medical evidence for life insurers (paramedical exams, tele-interviews, physician statements and lab tests), workplace drug testing and occupational health for employers, central laboratory services for clinical trials, genetic testing and sponsored companion diagnostics programs, and consumer services such as the results portal and self-pay tests. Insurers, employers, hospitals and drug companies pay by contract. Shared corporate functions (quality and accreditation, laboratory information systems and IT, finance and billing, the client contact centre, sales, supply chain, HR, legal and privacy, and facilities) support every line.

Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario and other provincial privacy commissioners

process_map.name: Register the patient and requisition at a collection centre
process_map.description: A lab assistant greets the patient, checks the requisition and health card, enters the ordering clinician, tests and patient details into the LIS and prints specimen labels. Uninsured tests are explained and paid at the counter. Handwritten or incomplete requisitions, unknown test names and expired health cards cause calls to the clinic and rework.
process_map.unit_of_work: one patient visit with its requisition

evidence.note: Visits per month are an estimate from 10 million patients a year.

process_map.name: Collect specimens at a collection centre
process_map.description: The lab assistant confirms identity with two identifiers, draws blood by venipuncture, collects or receives urine and other specimens, labels them at the chair and stores them at the required temperature for the next courier pickup. Difficult draws, fasting errors and mislabelled tubes are the main sources of recollection.

evidence.note: Same volume as registration.

process_map.name: Receive and accession specimens at the laboratory
process_map.description: Processing lab assistants open courier totes, reconcile them against manifests, check each specimen label against its requisition, complete accessioning in the LIS, centrifuge and aliquot, and sort tubes to benches or to other sites. Unlabelled, leaking, haemolysed or wrong-temperature specimens are rejected and logged, which triggers a recollection.

evidence.note: Specimen acceptability protocols are part of the QMS (src36).

process_map.name: Test specimens in chemistry, immunoassay and haematology
process_map.description: Technologists load specimens onto track-connected analysers, the middleware autoverifies most results against rules, and technologists review flagged results, reruns, delta checks and smears before release. Runs are released only after QC passes. Instrument downtime and reagent lots drive delays.
process_map.unit_of_work: one requisition with core laboratory tests (about five to six tests)

evidence.note: About 4.4 million tests a month in total across all disciplines (src4, src13).

process_map.name: Culture and identify organisms in microbiology
process_map.description: Lab assistants plate urine, swab and stool specimens; technologists read cultures over one to three days, identify organisms, run susceptibility tests and molecular panels, and report preliminary and final results. Positive reportable diseases are notified to public health.

evidence.note: Volume is an estimate (about 16 per cent of requisitions).

process_map.name: Screen Pap tests and other cytology
process_map.description: Liquid-based cytology slides are prepared and screened by cytotechnologists; negative cases are reported by the cytotechnologist and abnormal or unsatisfactory cases go to a pathologist. Screening rate limits and rescreening rules set the workload.

evidence.note: Volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Gross, process and cut tissue into slides
process_map.description: Pathologists' assistants gross biopsies, then histotechnologists process, embed, cut and stain the tissue and match slides to cases before delivery to the pathologist. Overnight processing sets a one-day minimum and recuts add time.

evidence.note: Duties from the histology MLT posting; volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Diagnose and sign out pathology cases
process_map.description: A pathologist reviews the slides with the clinical history, orders special stains or immunohistochemistry when needed, dictates the diagnosis, and signs the report after transcription. Second opinions and pending IHC lengthen turnaround.

evidence.note: More than 60 pathologists (src15); volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Report results to clinicians and LTC homes
process_map.description: Verified results flow from the LIS to clinicians' EMRs over HL7, to the eResults portal, or by fax and print, as interim and final cumulative reports, and are queued for the patient portal and billing. Staff work failed-delivery queues, amended reports and report copy requests.

evidence.note: One final report per community requisition.

process_map.name: Run and review daily quality control
process_map.description: Technologists run control materials on every analyser and test at the start of each run and at set intervals, the QC software applies rules, and failures stop patient reporting until troubleshooting, recalibration or repair. Charge technologists review shifts and trends monthly.

evidence.note: Quality control monitoring with software is part of the QMS (src36); count of analysers is an estimate.

process_map.name: Pick up and deliver specimens on scheduled courier routes
process_map.description: Couriers run fixed routes several times a day, collecting specimen bags from collection centres, physician offices, LTC teams and hospitals, scanning them into the tracking system and delivering them at the right temperature to the laboratory. Late stops, missed pickups and traffic cause specimens to miss the run.

evidence.note: Stops per month are an estimate from about 220 couriers.

process_map.name: Dispatch on-demand and STAT pickups
process_map.description: Dispatchers take calls and web requests for urgent pickups, assign the nearest courier, track the pickup to delivery and escalate delays. The service runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

evidence.note: Volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Move specimens between laboratories
process_map.description: Specimens needing tests done at another site (reference, genetics, toxicology, pathology) are packed to dangerous goods rules and moved by line haul or air freight with manifests and temperature control. Lost or delayed totes and temperature excursions are investigated.

evidence.note: Volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Deliver collection supplies to clinics and centres
process_map.description: Couriers deliver packed orders of tubes, containers, kits and requisitions to physician offices and collection centres on their routes. Wrong or short deliveries lead to calls and repeat runs.

evidence.note: Common practice for community labs; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Run custom courier services for healthcare clients
process_map.description: Hospitals and health organisations book custom deliveries of specimens, products and records through the web ordering system; dispatch assigns a courier, proof of delivery is captured, and the client is billed. Service level terms and after-hours requests make planning hard.

evidence.note: Volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Take LTC orders and schedule collection runs
process_map.description: Schedulers receive standing orders and new requisitions from long-term care and retirement homes, check them, enter or update them in the LIS, and build the next day's route of homes and residents for each mobile lab assistant. Late orders and changes from homes cause rescheduling.

evidence.note: Volume follows the LTC driver.

process_map.name: Collect specimens and ECGs in long-term care and retirement homes
process_map.description: A mobile lab assistant drives to each home, works with nursing staff to identify residents, draws blood, collects other specimens and records resting ECGs, labels specimens at the bedside and hands them to a courier or brings them to a drop point. Residents who refuse, are asleep or are not fasting cause missed draws.

evidence.note: Volume follows the LTC driver.

process_map.name: Book and perform private house calls
process_map.description: A patient or family books a home visit and pays a fee; the scheduler books a slot and a mobile lab assistant visits, registers the patient, collects specimens or an ECG and sends them to the laboratory. Travel time dominates the cost.

evidence.note: Volume follows the house call driver.

process_map.name: Send ECG tracings for interpretation and report
process_map.description: ECG tracings recorded in homes are transmitted to a contracted reading cardiologist, the interpretation is matched to the order and the report is delivered to the ordering physician. Missing patient data and late reads are the main issues.

evidence.note: Volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Receive and accession hospital referrals
process_map.description: Hospital laboratories send referral specimens with manifests or electronic orders; lab assistants check them against the manifest, accession them (often from the hospital LIS interface) and route them to the reference benches, molecular pathology or send-outs. Missing manifests and mismatched identifiers cause holds and calls.

evidence.note: Volume follows the hospital referral driver.

process_map.name: Perform specialised reference tests
process_map.description: Technologists run specialised chemistry, endocrinology, drug level and toxicology assays in batches on a schedule, review results with clinical scientists and release them. Batch schedules set turnaround, and low-volume assays need careful QC.

evidence.note: Includes hospital referrals and specialised community tests; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Manage send-outs to outside laboratories
process_map.description: Tests not done in-house are packaged and shipped to outside reference laboratories with requisitions, tracked until results return, and the results are entered or interfaced back for reporting. Outside invoices are matched and paid.

evidence.note: Common practice for reference laboratories; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Deliver reference results to hospitals
process_map.description: Results are sent to hospital LIS systems over bi-directional interfaces or through eResults, with reports for community-origin tests passed back to community reporting, and the work is queued for client billing. Coordinators chase interface errors and answer hospital result queries.

evidence.note: Volume matches reference testing.

process_map.name: Take and manage insurance medical evidence orders
process_map.description: Advisors and insurers place orders online, by email or phone; a case coordinator checks the requirements, creates the case in the Order Management System, assigns a health professional, books a tele-interview, requests the APS or inspection, and keeps iCARE status current. Incomplete applicant details and changing insurer requirements cause rework.

evidence.note: Volume follows the insurance orders driver.

process_map.name: Perform the paramedical exam
process_map.description: A health professional calls the applicant within 24 to 48 hours, books within 72 hours, visits the home or workplace, takes the health history, vitals, blood and urine and ECG as ordered, records it in ePara and ships the specimen kit. No-shows, rebookings and missing ECG equipment delay files.

evidence.note: Times and booking standards stated in src9; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Conduct insurance tele-interviews
process_map.description: A tele-interviewer calls the applicant at the booked time, asks the insurer's health, lifestyle and family history questions with reflex questions, records the answers in the questionnaire software and releases the report. A typical interview lasts about 25 minutes, and missed calls cause rebooking.

evidence.note: Length stated in src8; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Collect attending physician statements
process_map.description: An APS coordinator sends the insurer's request and the applicant's authorization to the attending physician by fax or portal, chases the clinic until the statement arrives, pays the physician's fee and releases the document. Waits on busy clinics make this the slowest evidence item.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Test insurance blood and urine profiles
process_map.description: Insurance specimen kits are received, matched to the Lab ID slip and order, tested on insurer profiles in the core laboratory, and results are reviewed and transmitted to the insurer within about 48 hours. Specimens are kept five weeks for repeat testing.

evidence.note: Turnaround and retention stated in src7; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Prepare inspection, motor vehicle and credit reports
process_map.description: Specialists interview applicants about finances, occupation and lifestyle, or obtain motor vehicle and credit records as the insurer requires, then write and release the report to the case. Waits on third-party record providers set the pace.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Review and release the evidence file to the insurer
process_map.description: When the ordered items are complete, a reviewer checks the file for missing signatures, values and documents, and the system transmits it to the insurer in ACORD or custom format, updates the advisor and queues the order for billing. Missing items reopen the case.

evidence.note: Volume follows orders.

process_map.name: Recruit, credential and pay health professionals
process_map.description: Network managers recruit and credential nurses and examiners, issue contracts, kits and equipment, monitor quality, and submit pay statements for completed visits to payables. Coverage gaps in rural areas are hard to fill.

evidence.note: Volume assumes about 900 contractors paid twice a month.

process_map.name: Set up an employer testing program
process_map.description: After a contract is signed, the program coordinator records the employer's policy, testing reasons, panels, cut-offs, random rates, designated contacts and reporting rules, and sets up accounts and collection sites. Scientists advise on panels and specimen types.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Order workplace tests and run random selections
process_map.description: Employers request pre-employment, post-incident and reasonable cause tests, and coordinators run random selections; the coordinator issues a donor authorization and directs the donor to a centre, an on-site collector or a third-party site. Urgent post-incident tests must be collected within hours.
process_map.unit_of_work: one drug or alcohol test request

evidence.note: Volume follows the drug test driver.

process_map.name: Collect chain of custody specimens
process_map.description: A certified collector verifies the donor's identity, follows the chain of custody procedure for urine or oral fluid with temperature and tamper checks, splits and seals the specimen, completes the custody form, and runs breath alcohol tests when ordered. Shy bladder cases and refusals follow set rules.

evidence.note: About 60 per cent of tests are assumed to be collected by company staff and 40 per cent by third-party sites.

process_map.name: Screen and confirm drug test specimens
process_map.description: The toxicology lab checks seals and custody forms, screens specimens by immunoassay, confirms non-negatives by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS, and a certifying scientist reviews the custody chain and data before release. Negatives are released within 6 to 24 hours and non-negatives need another 48 to 72 hours.

evidence.note: Turnaround stated in src27; volume from src12.

process_map.name: Medical review of non-negative results
process_map.description: A medical review officer reviews each non-negative or invalid result, contacts the donor to ask about prescriptions or other explanations, and verifies the result as negative or positive before it goes to the employer. Reaching donors takes repeated attempts.

evidence.note: MRO step is common practice; src26 describes official review of positives. Assumes about 7 per cent non-negative.

process_map.name: Report verified results to employers
process_map.description: Final results are posted to the employer's web reports or sent by secure fax to the designated representative, with periodic statistical and activity reports, and each test is queued for billing. Confidentiality rules limit who can receive results.

evidence.note: Volume follows the drug test driver.

process_map.name: Provide occupational health examinations
process_map.description: Occupational health nurses perform pre-employment, periodic and return-to-work examinations and collect specimens for trace metal, allergy and TB testing at centres or on site, then send the employer a fitness report. Results from the laboratory must arrive before the report is complete.

evidence.note: Volume follows the occupational exam driver.

process_map.name: Set up a clinical trial study
process_map.description: A project manager reviews the protocol, prepares the quote and lab manual, designs visit kits, has the LIS and trial system built for the study's tests and reference ranges, and agrees data formats with the sponsor. Protocol amendments restart parts of the build.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Build and ship trial kits to sites
process_map.description: Technicians assemble pre-labelled visit kits with tubes, requisitions and shipping materials, track expiry, and ship them to investigator sites on resupply requests. Expired kits and site stock-outs are the main issues.

evidence.note: Volume follows trial samples.

process_map.name: Receive, test and report trial samples
process_map.description: Samples arrive from sites by courier, are reconciled against the requisition and visit schedule, tested in the core or specialty laboratory, and reported to the site, with queries raised for missing or mismatched data. Protocol-specific alerts must be phoned to investigators.

evidence.note: Volume follows trial samples.

process_map.name: Store, transfer or destroy trial samples
process_map.description: Retained samples are logged into freezers by study and visit, shipped to the sponsor or another lab on request, or destroyed at the end of retention as the protocol allows. Freezer space and reconciliation take effort.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Transfer trial data to the sponsor
process_map.description: Data coordinators produce cumulative data files in the sponsor's format on the agreed schedule, reconcile them with the sponsor's database, resolve queries and close out the study, and the work is queued for billing. Format changes and reconciliation queries cause rework.
process_map.unit_of_work: one monthly data transfer for one study

evidence.note: One transfer per active study a month; estimate.

process_map.name: Perform genetic and specialised tests
process_map.description: Orders for prenatal screening, carrier screening, hereditary and pharmacogenomic tests are checked for consent and payment, DNA is extracted, tests are run and analysed, and a laboratory geneticist signs the report. Private-pay tests are invoiced to patients, and complex variants take longer to interpret.

evidence.note: Volume follows the genetic orders driver.

process_map.name: Provide genetic counselling and pharmacogenomic consults
process_map.description: Genetic counsellors and clinical pharmacists explain results and options to patients and clinicians by phone or video, and send a summary letter. Booking and reaching patients takes time.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Run IHC and molecular tests on tissue
process_map.description: Technologists cut and stain tissue blocks for immunohistochemistry, ISH and mutation tests such as KRAS, and the results are interpreted and reported to the pathologist or the program. Block retrieval from other labs and repeat staining add delays.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Run sponsored companion diagnostics programs
process_map.description: For each sponsor program, coordinators enrol patients referred by specialists, arrange appointments and specimen pickup, track testing, deliver the biomarker report to the physician and send the sponsor de-identified program reports and invoices. Each program has its own rules and reporting.

evidence.note: Volume follows the companion diagnostics driver.

process_map.name: Book collection centre appointments online
process_map.description: Patients book a time at a collection centre online or by phone, receive reminders, and may upload their requisition in advance; the booking feeds the centre's queue. No-shows and walk-ins make capacity planning hard.

evidence.note: About 57 per cent of visits assumed booked.

process_map.name: Register patients for the results portal
process_map.description: A patient signs up for the consumer health service, verifies identity, pays the subscription, and the account is matched to the patient's laboratory record. Identity mismatches need agent help.

evidence.note: Subscription of $9.99 a year (src37); volume estimate.

process_map.name: Release results to the patient portal
process_map.description: Results for registered patients are published to the portal with plain-language explanations and trends after release rules (such as delays for sensitive tests) are applied; patients with questions are routed to support or their clinician, and the portal offers referrals to virtual care and therapy partners.

evidence.note: Volume follows the portal driver.

process_map.name: Sell self-pay tests online
process_map.description: A patient buys a test online, pays by card, receives a requisition and visits a centre for collection, or receives an at-home kit; genetic and pharmacogenomic tests go to the genetics lab. Results go to the portal.

evidence.note: Volume follows the self-pay driver.

process_map.name: Answer patient and clinician inquiries
process_map.description: Customer care representatives answer calls and messages in English and French about results, locations, requisitions, preparation and billing, look up records in the LIS, request report copies and pass complaints to patient relations. Peaks in the morning drive wait times.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Phone critical results to clinicians
process_map.description: When a result passes critical limits, the technologist confirms it and a call attendant phones the ordering clinician or on-call physician, documents read-back, time and person, and escalates to a medical director if no one can be reached. After-hours calls to clinics that are closed are the hard part.

evidence.note: The provider page links to alert reporting guidelines (src5); about 0.35 per cent of requisitions assumed critical.

process_map.name: Handle complaints and patient relations
process_map.description: Patient relations specialists log complaints about service, billing or results, investigate with the site or department, respond in writing or by phone, and open nonconformances for system problems.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Run proficiency testing
process_map.description: Quality staff receive blind samples from proficiency testing programs, technologists test them like patient samples, results are submitted on time, and graded reports are reviewed with any failure investigated.

evidence.note: EQA programs (CAP, QMP-LS and others) listed in src36; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Prepare for and host accreditation assessments
process_map.description: Quality managers prepare documents and self-assessments, host the assessors on site, and submit corrective action evidence for findings by the deadline. Each laboratory faces several programs (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics, CAP, MANQAP, SAMHSA).

evidence.note: Frequency estimate from about 9 labs and several programs on two to four year cycles.

process_map.name: Manage nonconformances and corrective actions
process_map.description: Staff log QC failures, rejected specimens, complaints, proficiency failures and audit findings; quality specialists assign investigation, root cause and corrective action, check effectiveness and close the record.

evidence.note: Preventive and corrective action programs listed in src36; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Hold quality management review
process_map.description: Each quarter, quality and operations leaders review quality indicators such as specimen rejection and turnaround, CAPA status, audit and proficiency results and complaints, and agree actions and resources that feed the strategic plan. Gathering data from many sites takes most of the effort.

evidence.note: Management review listed in src36.

process_map.name: Validate and introduce new tests
process_map.description: When a new test or method is approved, the validation analyst and technologists plan and run accuracy, precision and reference interval studies, the medical director approves the report, and the LIS build and procedures are completed before go-live.

evidence.note: Validation and change control listed in src36; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Train staff and assess competency
process_map.description: New and existing staff are trained on procedures and assessed yearly for each task they perform, with records kept in the QMS. Staff cannot work unsupervised until signed off.

evidence.note: Training and competency assessments listed in src36; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Build and change the LIS and interfaces
process_map.description: LIS analysts build new tests, rules, client codes and EMR or hospital interfaces from approved requests, test them in a validation environment and move them to production under change control. Backlogs delay new tests and client go-lives.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Resolve IT incidents and requests
process_map.description: The service desk logs calls from staff and clinics (printers, label printers, EMR result delivery, passwords), resolves what it can and escalates the rest to infrastructure or LIS teams.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Operate infrastructure and security monitoring
process_map.description: Engineers patch and back up servers and networks across about 200 sites, monitor security alerts and handle escalated incidents; suspected breaches go to the privacy office.
process_map.unit_of_work: one infrastructure change or security event

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Grant and review system access
process_map.description: New users get accounts and roles in the LIS and other systems on request from HR, leavers are removed, and access logs are reviewed for inappropriate viewing of patient records.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Bill provincial health plans
process_map.description: Completed community requisitions are coded and submitted electronically to OHIP and Manitoba Health; billing clerks fix rejected claims (invalid health numbers, unlicensed tests), reconcile remittances, and track billing against the company's annual Ontario funding cap.

evidence.note: Cap and per-test payment described in src23 and src39; about 85 per cent of community requisitions assumed provincially billed.

process_map.name: Bill and collect from patients
process_map.description: Patients pay at centres or online for uninsured tests, Quebec community tests, house calls, private-pay genetics and portal subscriptions; clerks reconcile point-of-sale and online payments, issue receipts for private insurance claims and chase unpaid invoices.

evidence.note: Quebec patient-pay for private community labs is common knowledge but not confirmed by an opened source; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Invoice clients and collect receivables
process_map.description: Billable work for hospitals, insurers, employers, trial sponsors, program sponsors and courier clients is priced by contract, invoiced monthly or per case, and collected, with disputes and credit notes handled by collections clerks.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Pay suppliers and contractors
process_map.description: Payables clerks match supplier invoices to purchase orders and receipts, process contractor, outside laboratory and physician fee statements, route exceptions for approval and pay in weekly runs. Invoices without a purchase order or receipt wait for approvers.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume follows the supplier invoice driver.

process_map.name: Close the books each month
process_map.description: Accountants post accruals for unbilled tests and unpaid invoices, reconcile billing, receivables, payables and payroll, estimate provincial cap adjustments, and produce monthly results in the parent company's format and tight timetable.

evidence.note: Common practice for a subsidiary of a listed company.

process_map.name: Prepare the annual budget and forecasts
process_map.description: FP&A builds the annual budget and quarterly forecasts by business line, including volumes, the Ontario funding cap, headcount and capital, and submits it to the parent.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Run payroll
process_map.description: Payroll administrators process hires, changes, hours and leave from the HRIS and scheduling system every two weeks, run payroll and post it to the ledger.

evidence.note: Common practice; biweekly pay assumed.

process_map.name: Manage physician and clinic accounts
process_map.description: Territory account managers visit physician practices and clinics, set up new accounts, resolve service problems, promote tests and pass requests for new tests to the medical team.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Onboard new clients
process_map.description: A new client is set up with an LIS client code, EMR or hospital interface, eResults access, courier stop and starter supplies. Delays in interface work hold up go-live.

evidence.note: Volume follows the new accounts driver.

process_map.name: Win hospital, insurer, employer and sponsor contracts
process_map.description: National sales teams answer RFPs and negotiate contracts with hospitals, insurers, employers and trial sponsors, with legal review of terms and pricing approval before signing.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Contract with reagent and instrument suppliers
process_map.description: Procurement runs tenders and negotiates multi-year reagent rental, instrument and consumables agreements within the budget, often aligned with parent company contracts, with laboratory and quality staff judging technical fit. Changing a supplier needs new test validation.

evidence.note: Purchasing control listed in src36; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Replenish inventory and receive goods
process_map.description: Buyers raise purchase orders from stock requisitions and minimum levels, warehouse staff receive and inspect deliveries, and receipts are passed to payables. Backorders force substitutions that need validation.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Pick and pack collection supplies and kits
process_map.description: Distribution clerks pick and pack orders of tubes, containers, requisitions and insurance kits for clinics, centres and contracted health professionals, and hand them to couriers or mail.

evidence.note: Volume estimate.

process_map.name: Recruit staff
process_map.description: Recruiters post approved positions, screen applicants, arrange interviews with hiring managers, check credentials such as CMLTO registration, driving abstracts and vulnerable sector checks, and issue offers. Shortages of technologists and lab assistants keep many roles open.

evidence.note: About 140 open roles at once (src32); hires a month is an estimate.

process_map.name: Onboard new employees
process_map.description: HR coordinators set up the employee in the HRIS and payroll, collect forms and credentials, request system access, and schedule orientation, privacy training and job training so the person can be signed off as competent.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Manage workplace injuries and return to work
process_map.description: Needlestick, lifting and vehicle incidents are reported, investigated and filed with the compensation board, and injured staff are supported back to work with modified duties; employee relations cases follow a similar path.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Respond to privacy incidents
process_map.description: Suspected breaches such as misdirected reports, lost specimens with labels or inappropriate access are contained, investigated and assessed; affected people are notified and reportable breaches are filed with the privacy commissioner.

evidence.note: Common practice under provincial health privacy law; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Handle record requests and privacy audits
process_map.description: Privacy analysts respond to patient requests for copies of their records within legal time limits, review access audit logs for inappropriate viewing, and complete privacy impact assessments for new systems and partners, reporting status to leadership.

evidence.note: Common practice; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Maintain licences and certifications
process_map.description: Compliance and regulatory staff file licence renewals and changes for laboratories and collection centres, keep SAMHSA and other certifications current, and report compliance status to leadership.

evidence.note: Licences listed in src36; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Maintain and repair laboratory instruments
process_map.description: Technologists do daily and weekly maintenance, biomedical technicians coordinate preventive maintenance, calibration and repairs with vendor field service, and instruments return to service only after QC passes.

evidence.note: Equipment control program in src36; routine maintenance duty in src33; volume estimate.

process_map.name: Open, move or refit collection centres
process_map.description: Facilities lease and fit out new or relocated centres, arrange licensing with the regulator and hand the site to operations. Landlord delays and licence approvals set the timeline.

evidence.note: New centre openings appear in the news list (src4); volume estimate.

process_map.name: Set strategy and annual plan
process_map.description: The executive team reviews performance, quality, market changes and parent company targets and sets priorities such as acquisitions, new tests and site changes for the coming years.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Review monthly business performance
process_map.description: Each month the executive team and business line leaders review volumes, turnaround, quality, compliance and financial results against budget, agree corrective actions, and send a performance report to the parent company.

evidence.note: Common practice.

process_map.name: Negotiate provincial funding agreements
process_map.description: Executives negotiate community laboratory funding agreements, price changes and cap allocations with the Ontario Ministry of Health, sign the agreement and pass the terms to billing and planning. Funding is set per company and changes rarely.

evidence.note: Transfer payment agreements and company caps described in src24, src39 and src23.

assumptions: Reference period 2019-2022. The British Columbia laboratories acquired in 2023 and the 2026 Laval laboratory and at-home tests are outside the period and are not modelled. COVID-19 testing volumes in 2020-2022 are not modelled as a separate process; they would raise collection, logistics, testing and billing volumes temporarily.
Employees are set at 3,300 (February 2022, src22). Role headcounts sum to about 3,100; the gap stands for casual, float and student staff not assigned to a role.
Most of the 1,200+ mobile health professionals (src13) are treated as contractors paid per visit and shown as an outside party; only about 60 employed examiners are counted as staff.

Loaded cost per hour is hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead). Wages come from Job Bank Ontario medians and ranges (src28 to src31) and one posted the model laboratory range (src33); other wages are the author's estimates.
Unit headcounts are computed from the role headcounts in each subtree, so they always add up; they are estimates, not published figures.

Monthly volumes are derived from the stated scale (10 million patients a year, 40,000 specimens a day, 50 to 55 million tests a year, 300,000 drug tests a year) and divided among processes by the author's judgement. Only the drivers marked tier A rest directly on a stated number.

Quebec community laboratory testing at private labs is assumed to be paid by patients (often reimbursed by private insurance); no opened source confirmed this, so the patient billing process is tier C.
Laboratory testing for insurers and clinical trials is done by technologists in the shared core laboratory; those processes are owned by their business lines and list core laboratory roles.
The medical review officer is modelled as a contracted, part-time physician role in workplace services. The website does not describe MRO services, so this is tier C common practice.
Critical result calls are assigned to the client services results call desk (call attendants), with technologists and medical directors involved; the actual split in the company is not public.
One executive (vice president, corporate client solutions) is assumed to oversee workplace, clinical trials and genetics; the real reporting lines above director level are not public.

Insurance specimens and trial samples arrive by commercial or overnight courier directly to the laboratory; only community, hospital and inter-site movements are routed through the company's own courier processes.
